body:
I've created this issue because I'd like to discuss `packspec` integration in `vim.pack` (neovim/neovim#34778) to make sure the scope sounds reasonable and discuss `packspec` related questions. Here is the outline of what I currently think is the path forward:

1. Add a new field to `vim.pack.get()` outputs with the contents of 'pkg.json' file.

2. Update install+update+delete functionality to autosource (with appropriately adjusted `'cwd'` and `'runtimepath'`) scripts declared in 'pkg.json':

    - `scripts.install` after triggering `PackChanged kind=install`. The reason to execute after triggering event (here and in all other cases) is so that there is a possibility for users to execute code both before the script (exactly on event) and after the script (more-or-less via `vim.schedule` called on the event).
    - `scripts.preupdate` after triggering `PackChangedPre kind=update`.
    - `scripts.update` after triggering `PackChanged kind=update`.
    - `scripts.preuninstall` after triggering `PackChangedPre kind=delete` (although [`npm` does not support it](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v9/using-npm/scripts#a-note-on-a-lack-of-npm-uninstall-scripts), I think it is still a valid field which is useful for `vim.pack`).

    Extra question: should there be "disable" and/or "trust" mechanism? Probably not, as there is none for 'plugin/' scripts.

3. Include some **very light** recognition of "dependency plugins" with the idea that requiring users to explicitly add every plugin to their config is a good long-term UX. I.e. no transitive auto-install (less prone to security attacks, less `vim.pack` code to maintain, etc.) or complicated resolution of best version (less `vim.pack` code).

    The general scope comes down to:
    - Store dependency data in the lockfile to be able to quickly do some useful things:
        - Before loading a plugin, warn if there is a dependency that is not loaded.
        - Install/update from the lockfile in "dependencies come first" order.
    - Provide more thorough checks in `:checkhealth vim.pack`.

4. Update `:checkhealth vim.pack` to include the following checks:

    - Neovim version (from `engines.nvim` 'pkg.json' field).

    - All "dependency plugins" are installed and have user-declared `version` (via `vim.pack.add()`) compatible with what's asked in 'pkg.json'.

5. No recognition of the `name` field of 'pkg.json', as it is tricky. Using plugin's 'pack/core/opt/*' directory name and allowing users to configure it proved to be good enough.

---

Based on the above, I think the following needs discussions and decisions:

1. Documentation in `:h vim.pack`. In particular:

    - There needs to be a name for 'pkg.json' file. Just when writing this issue it was a bit awkward to use "'pkg.json' field/file".  The common one seems to be "plugin manifest file", but I haven't seen this used here. So it would be `:h vim.pack-manifest` tag and `manifest` field in `vim.pack.get()` output, for example.

    - Should `:h vim.pack` be the main source for "all things manifest file related" or linking to [`https://github.com/neovim/packspec`](https://github.com/neovim/packspec) is enough? Or a combination of both?

2. The shape of hook fields in the manifest file. It looks like `scripts.*` with specific pre-determined names (listed above) is pretty much established.

3. The shape of dependencies. This doesn't look agreed upon yet. Here are the requirements for `vim.pack`: there needs to be a way for a plugin to declare that it needs a *dependency plugins* that *can be installed via `vim.pack` at a particular version*. This means that there needs to be ways to:

    - Define that a particular dependency is a plugin (not a library, executable, etc.).

    - Define that a particular dependency is installed via Git (not `curl`, `pacman`, etc.)

    - Define a version that is compatible with `vim.pack`. I.e. version range, Git branch/tag/commit.

Building on top of [tl;dr from README](https://github.com/neovim/packspec#tldr), [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues/41#issuecomment-4891600015), and how `vim.pack.add()`+lockfile work, here is an example of my manifest file suggestion:

```json
{
  "name": "neoplugin",
  "description": "The best Neovim plugin",
  "engines": {
    "nvim": ">=0.12.0", // Will be used in `:checkhealth vim.pack`
    "vim": ">=9.1.0"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "install": "scripts/install.lua",
    "preupdate": "scripts/preupdate.vim",
    "update": "scripts/update.vim",
    "preuninstall": "scripts/preuninstall.lua"
  },
  "packspec": {
    "dependencies": [ // Use array to make it similar to `vim.pack.add`
                      // Also adds extra information about loading order
      "https://github.com/user/plugin1", // Allow string
      {
        "src": "https://github.com/user/plugin2" // Allow table with only `src`
        // "version" may be skipped with "default branch" as default
      },
      {
        "src": "https://github.com/user/plugin3",
        "version": ">=1.0.0" // Allow version ranges
      },
      {
        "src": "https://github.com/user/plugin4",
        "version": "'develop'" // Allow "'...'" to define branch/commit/tag
      },
      {
        "src": "https://github.com/user/plugin5",
        "type": "plugin", // May be skipped, but requires `"plugin"` to be default
        "protocol": "git" // May be skipped, but requires `"git"` to be default
      },
    ]
  }
}
```

Notes:

- I'd ask to drop the extra `"packspec"` nesting. It feels confusing while the potential benefit of reusing `npm` registries will likely not realize. An alternative is to make it explicit that `"packspec"` defines data that `packspec`-compatible plugin manager must recognize. In this case, `"type"` and `"protocol"` are not necessary for `vim.pack` to work.

- I think using an array for dependencies makes more sense. Both in terms of alignment with `vim.pack` and in general. This adds an extra information about potential order of plugins, which is nice.

- Any top-level field is optional. In dependencies only `src` (if table) is required, others are optional (with defaults ``).

comment_data.body:
which parts of this (if any) conflict with the plan in https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues/41#issuecomment-1616017735 ?

which parts resolve open questions?

which parts deviate from npm package.json ?

> which parts of this (if any) conflict with the plan in [#41 (comment)](https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues/41#issuecomment-1616017735) ?
> 
> which parts resolve open questions?
> 
> which parts deviate from npm package.json ?

#41 doesn't touch on the general outline of how `vim.pack` will use manifest file. This is half of this issue.

#41 doesn't touch on the general name of 'pkg.json' file.

#41 mentions "uninstall" hook/script as out of scope, which I think is too much as it is useful and doesn't seem to contradict with `npm` format.

The [linked comment](https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues/41#issuecomment-1616017735) itself is outdated with respect to how to define dependencies. This issue proposes a more flexible shape in light of [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/packspec/issues/41#issuecomment-4891600015).

> * Include some **very light** recognition of "dependency plugins" ...
>   * Store dependency data in the lockfile to be able to quickly do some useful things:
>     * Before loading a plugin, warn if there is a dependency that is not loaded.
>     * Install/update from the lockfile in "dependencies come first" order.
>   * Provide more thorough checks in `:checkhealth vim.pack`.

would this be like vscode's "extension packs"? i.e., a flat list of deps.

> Install/update from the lockfile in "dependencies come first"

Establishing a deterministic order definitely seems valuable, and I wouldn't even frame it as "supporting dependencies".

However, this might have implications for how `vim.pack.add()` works?

> warn if there is a dependency that is not loaded

I guess "light recognition" sounds _ok_, but I wonder if it makes sense for Nvim's `require()` / loader to be smarter on failure? I.e. it could dig around in the runtimepath, and maybe read the `vim.pack` / packspec tree.

IOW, this would be a loader feature, for all packages, not just "dependency plugins".



> 5\. No recognition of the `name` field of 'pkg.json', as it is tricky

I also wasn't sure about that. I do like the idea of avoiding it.

> 5\. Using plugin's 'pack/core/opt/*' directory name and allowing users to configure it proved to be good enough.

I'm really leaning towards using `plugin/<name>.lua` as the formal plugin name, and requiring all plugins to provide that (and fallback to something derived from the path otherwise). This will be needed for prefixing messages, too.

> * There needs to be a name for 'pkg.json' file

What's wrong with `pkg.json` ? It's clear and unambiguous.

> * Should `:h vim.pack` be the main source for "all things manifest file related" or linking to [`https://github.com/neovim/packspec`](https://github.com/neovim/packspec) is enough? Or a combination of both?

I'm in favor of linking, but a vimdoc `packspec.txt` would also be good, but ideally we would generate it from this repo.



> 2\. The shape of hook fields in the manifest file. It looks like `scripts.*` with specific pre-determined names (listed above) is pretty much established.

yes 👍 



> * I'd ask to drop the extra `"packspec"` nesting.

yes 👍  let's go ahead and do that.

when testing compat with npm package.json, we can have a small script that converts our `dependencies` format to package.json format. that allows us to use their validation as the source of truth.



> I think using an array for dependencies makes more sense. Both in terms of alignment with `vim.pack` and in general. This adds an extra information about potential order of plugins, which is nice.

A dict makes sense if transitive deps are supported. Otherwise an (ordered) array makes more sense, and actually emphasizes the lack of transitive deps. 👍 

## TODO


- update packspec to mention the `dependencies` format above
- update validator and add CI task

> However, this might have implications for how vim.pack.add() works?

It probably will, but I don't think it would be crucial in cases where it doesn't matter. The only time I currently see this matter is during first install from the lockfile. Right now all plugins are installed in alphabetical order, but with present `deps` field in the lockfile those plugins will be installed and get their hooks (from `pkg.json`) executed before the "main" plugin. The order of dependencies in the "main" plugin's `pkg.json` will determine their order of installation and hook executions. There might be edge cases when several plugins define dependencies in different order, but I think just picking the first order and reporting the potential problem in `:checkhealth vim.pack` should be enough.

> I guess "light recognition" sounds ok, but I wonder if it makes sense for Nvim's require() / loader to be smarter on failure? I.e. it could dig around in the runtimepath, and maybe read the vim.pack / packspec tree.

This might be useful, but my first impression is that adds more complexity than it solves issues.

> What's wrong with pkg.json ? It's clear and unambiguous.

Mostly because it feels awkward to use in the documentation and Lua table fields. Compare:
- `:h vim.pack-pkg.json`, "Plugins can come with a `pkg.json` file (located at top level)", `vim.pack.get()[1]['pkg.json']`.
- `:h vim.pack-manifest`, "Plugins can come with a manifest file (top level `pkg.json`)", `vim.pack.get()[1].manifest`.

> * `:h vim.pack-manifest`, "Plugins can come with a manifest file (top level `pkg.json`)", `vim.pack.get()[1].manifest`.

that LGTM. as long as we say "pkg.json" in most other places. "the manifest file" is something that will be less intuitive for many people reading docs. but as a field name, sure, `manifest` is fine and most users won't be interacting with that.
